title: Turn a pizza in place on an oven deck and return its peel to the rack
instruction: Turn the pizza half a turn with the turning peel, keeping it centered on the oven deck. Leave it topping-side up and put the peel back on both supports.
context: Pizza cooks rotate a partially baked crust in a confined oven to change which edge faces the heat. The turning peel can push the crust sideways or slide beneath it while the toppings stay clear.
setup: A 300 mm, 283 g pizza rests on a 480 × 780 mm stone deck inside a 130 mm high opening. A 400 g turning peel has a 170 mm metal blade, a 16 mm wide shaft and a textured grip. The blade lies on the front shelf and the shaft rests between 5 mm lips on a rear support 340 mm behind it. Two YAM arms and the oven share one fixed countertop layout.
scoring: Turn the pizza by contacting its side or underside. Credited net turns of at least 45, 90 and 135 degrees earn 0.2, 0.4 and 0.6. A net turn of 175–185 degrees with 165 degrees of credited progress earns 0.8. Reach 1.0 by releasing the aligned, level peel on both supports for 3 s with at most 2 mm drift. Exceeding 50 mm center excursion or 15 degrees pizza tilt, losing deck contact, or directly touching the pizza with the robot scores zero. The README specifies contact thresholds. Turning by rubbing the pizza top earns no rotation credit.
reset_notes: Reset to the fixed intact scene, with both grippers open and the peel on the rack.
fidelity: Rigid metal peel with passive contact, rigid stone, a set-crust center with 16 flexible rim segments and 12 compression pads. Attached toppings indicate orientation. Simulated material coefficients, cutaway view, no thermal or physical-hardware validation.
scores: YAM demo: 1.0 with the current grader. Dream-1 video: original live run, 0.0 under the previous grader (5,000 actions). Offline replay of those same 5,000 recorded actions with the current grader: 0.0.
